title: Spec of the square-zero algebra $K[\epsilon_1,\dots,\epsilon_n]$ is the pushout of $n$ copies of the dual-number scheme
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $K[\epsilon]$ the dual numbers over $K$ [def-sc-dual-numbers], and $n\ge1$. Let $K[\epsilon_1,\dots,\epsilon_n]$ be the $K$-algebra with basis $1,\epsilon_1,\dots,\epsilon_n$ and $\epsilon_i\epsilon_j=0$ for all $i,j$. For $i=1,\dots,n$ let $j_i:\operatorname{Spec}K[\epsilon]\to\operatorname{Spec}K[\epsilon_1,\dots,\epsilon_n]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] be $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the $K$-algebra map with $\epsilon_i\mapsto\epsilon$ and $\epsilon_l\mapsto0$ for $l\ne i$, and let $c:\operatorname{Spec}K\to\operatorname{Spec}K[\epsilon]$ be $\operatorname{Spec}$ of the map $\epsilon\mapsto0$. Then for every scheme $X$ and morphisms of schemes $\theta_1,\dots,\theta_n:\operatorname{Spec}K[\epsilon]\to X$ with $\theta_1\circ c=\dots=\theta_n\circ c$, there is a unique morphism of schemes $\Theta:\operatorname{Spec}K[\epsilon_1,\dots,\epsilon_n]\to X$ with $\Theta\circ j_i=\theta_i$ for $i=1,\dots,n$; that is, $\operatorname{Spec}K[\epsilon_1,\dots,\epsilon_n]$ with the $j_i$ is the wide pushout of $n$ copies of $c$ in the category of schemes.

source.place: Tag 0B2B, varieties-lemma-tangent-space (pushout of dual-number thickenings, via Schemes Lemma 01J6 on morphisms from spectra of local rings)

proof.text: Write $D=K[\epsilon]$ and $A_n=K[\epsilon_1,\dots,\epsilon_n]$. Every element of $A_n$ has a unique expression $a+\sum_i b_i\epsilon_i$. The maps defining $j_i$ identify $A_n$ with the ring of tuples $(a_i+b_i\epsilon)_i\in D^n$ whose constant terms $a_i$ all agree: the inverse sends such a tuple to $a+\sum_i b_i\epsilon_i$, and both multiplication laws give constant coefficient $aa'$ and $i$th infinitesimal coefficient $ab_i'+a'b_i$. Thus $A_n$ is the finite fibre product of the quotient maps $D\to K$. In each ring $D$ and $A_n$, the ideal of infinitesimals is square-zero and the quotient is the field $K$; consequently each is local, with its unique closed point given by that ideal. This is the ring calculation invoked in Stacks Tag 0B2B, extended from two factors to finite $n$.

Let $z$ be the common morphism $\theta_i\circ c:\operatorname{Spec}K\to X$. Under [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring], write $z$ as a point $x\in X$ and a local ring map $\psi:\mathcal O_{X,x}\to K$. The same correspondence writes each $\theta_i$ as $(x_i,\varphi_i)$ with $\varphi_i:\mathcal O_{X,x_i}\to D$. Since the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}K$ maps under $c$ to the closed point of $\operatorname{Spec}D$, equality $\theta_i\circ c=z$ gives $x_i=x$; compatibility of stalk maps under composition gives $D\to K$ composed with $\varphi_i$ equal to $\psi$. By step 1, the tuple $(\varphi_i)_i$ therefore defines a unique ring map $\varphi:\mathcal O_{X,x}\to A_n$ whose $i$th projection is $\varphi_i$. Its residue map is $\psi$, so it is local. Apply the correspondence again to $(x,\varphi)$ to obtain $\Theta:\operatorname{Spec}A_n\to X$.

For each $i$, both $\Theta\circ j_i$ and $\theta_i$ correspond under [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-local-ring] to $(x,\varphi_i)$, because the map on the closed-point local rings induced by $j_i$ is the $i$th projection $A_n\to D$; hence they are equal. Conversely, any $\Theta'$ with these restrictions corresponds to a point $x'$ and a local map $\varphi':\mathcal O_{X,x'}\to A_n$. Restricting along one $j_i$ gives $x'=x$, and restricting along all of them gives the projections of $\varphi'$ equal to the $\varphi_i$. The coefficient description in step 1 makes the projections jointly injective, so $\varphi'=\varphi$ and the correspondence yields $\Theta'=\Theta$. For $n=1$ the calculation is the identity $A_1=D$, and for $n=2$ it is precisely the pushout asserted in Tag 0B2B.
